Raw Throughput (No Wait States)

Objective

The goal of this benchmark was to measure the maximum execution throughput of TaktX on a trivial BPMN process without any wait states. This test represents the upper bound of the engine’s raw performance and scalability.

 

Test setup

  • Kafka: DigitalOcean Managed Cluster (3×2 vCPU Premium), replication factor = 2
  • Engine nodes: 1 and 2 nodes (4 vCPU, 8GB memory each)
  • Kafka Streams threads: 2–6 per node
  • Process starter: 1 node, 4 vCPU, 1 thread
  • Durability: acks=all, idempotence=true
  • Other: Kafka batch=262,144, linger=50 ms, commit interval=100 ms, poll=50 ms

Tests were run by starting 1,000,000 process instances as fast as possible. I measured the time until no more consumer lag was visible indicating that all process instances were finished.

Results

Key takeaways:

  • Single-node ceiling (with broadcast): ~71k PI/s @ 6 partitions, 6 streams threads, 4 client threads.
  • Two-node scaling: With 12 partitions, ~111k PI/s (broadcast on). That’s a strong scale-up over the 1-node result, limited mainly by Kafka/partition parallelism rather than CPU.
  • Headless mode: Turning oﬀ exports/broadcast lifts this to ~143k PI/s on the same 2-node setup, showing that observability adds measurable but moderate overhead.
  • Threads vs partitions: At 3 partitions, increasing Streams threads from 4→6 doesn’t help (same 62.5k PI/s), confirming the partition count was the limiter there. Gains resume when moving to 6 and 12 partitions.
  • Durability still on: Even with acks=all and idempotence=true, throughput remains six-figure PI/s on modest hardware.
